## Introduction

For this assignment, I will be using the pivot functions in the TidyVerse Package.

As an example, I use the [Our World in Data energy dataset](https://github.com/owid/energy-data),
which reports what share of each country's electricity comes from each source
(coal, gas, solar, wind and so on).

## Load the Data

The data is read straight from a public URL, so no local file is needed.

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(ggplot2)

energy <- read_csv(
  "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/owid/energy-data/master/owid-energy-data.csv",
  show_col_types = FALSE
)

dim(energy)
```

The dataset has over 100 columns. I keep the country, the year and the eight
columns that give each individual source's share of electricity
generation.

```{r}
countries <- c("United States", "Germany", "United Kingdom", "China", "India")

elec_wide <- energy |>
  filter(country %in% countries, year >= 1990) |>
  select(
    country, year,
    coal_share_elec, gas_share_elec, oil_share_elec, nuclear_share_elec,
    hydro_share_elec, wind_share_elec, solar_share_elec,
    biofuel_share_elec
  )

head(elec_wide)
```

This data is in wide formatting, so I will use the pivot longer function.

```{r}
elec_long <- elec_wide |>
  pivot_longer(
    cols = ends_with("_share_elec"),
    names_to = "source",
    names_pattern = "(.*)_share_elec",
    values_to = "share"
  )

head(elec_long, 10)
```

Some countries do not report every source in every year. Long data makes it
easy to see exactly where the gaps are:


## Data Visualization


```{r}
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 6

elec_long |>
  mutate(source = fct_reorder(source, share, .fun = mean, .desc = TRUE)) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = year, y = share, fill = source)) +
  geom_area() +
  facet_wrap(~ country) +
  labs(
    title = "Share of Electricity Generation by Source, 1990 onward",
    x = NULL,
    y = "Share of electricity (%)",
    fill = "Source",
    caption = "Source: Our World in Data"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```
